Subject: Capacity options and ramp cadence for AureonThera pilot

Emma — following up from last week's demo. Attached is a compact worksheet describing three reservation options that map to the pilot and a likely production trajectory. High-level options (see attached xlsx for numbers and cost model):

- Conservative Pilot (30 days):
  - Cluster: 1 x 8-GPU pool (A100-80GB equiv) dedicated
  - Min GPUs guaranteed: 4 (reserved) / burst to 8 for short windows
  - Ramp: 0% -> 30% over week 1, 60% by week 3, review at day 30
  - Purpose: smoke-test inference flows, tune batching and KV cache

- Growth Slate (90 days):
  - Cluster: 1 x 24-GPU pool (multi-node)
  - Min GPUs guaranteed: 12 with scheduled burst capacity to 20
  - Ramp cadence: weekly increments tied to token throughput (10% increments)
  - Purpose: steady-state feature validation and user-facing latency targets

- Anchored Production (12+ months):
  - Cluster: 2 x 40-GPU pools (regionally distributed)
  - Min GPUs guaranteed: 30 (reserve) with warm standby in a second region
  - Ramp: phased over 3 months with canary traffic and automated fallback to smaller model variants if SLAs slip

Key notes:
- Warm-up credits: we include a one-time warm-up allowance (equivalent to 48 hours of full load) to pre-populate KV/prefix caches.
- Billing: pilot priced as a time-boxed reserved lane with blended unit rates; growth and production are tiered commits with overage caps.
- Measurement triggers: we propose explicit check-ins (7d, 30d, 90d) and a token-based cost runway model so you can see projection vs actual.

I've attached the spreadsheet which includes per-model GPU counts, expected p50/p95 latencies at 2k seq and cost projections. If helpful I can convert the cost model to your procurement format.

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment this week to pick an option and lock the PoC start date. Available: Wed 10:00–12:00 or Thu 14:00–16:00 PT.

Emma — good questions; answers inline below and I attached a PoC agenda PDF to help procurement and engineering align.

1) Conservative Pilot minimum: the 4-GPU minimum is a guaranteed reserve for the primary chat model (2k seq); we recommend leaving 1–2 GPUs as headroom for reranker traffic, which can be handled via burst windows. If you expect both models to be hot simultaneously at p95, bump the reserved to 6.

2) Growth Slate minimum term: pricing steps down after a 60-day committed window inside the 90-day slate; we give a mid-slate true-up at day 60 where we can convert partial credits into a longer monthly commit if you want to smooth billing.

3) SLO & escalation: we maintain 99.5% availability on Dedicated lanes at the per-request level (regional), 200ms median token latency target for 2k sequences on Anchored Production. Escalation path: AE -> CS Lead -> Infra SRE -> Exec on-call; I'll include a one-page SLO doc in the next thread.

Proposed refinement to ramp: start pilot with 4 reserved (6 operational, 2 for burst) for 14 days, then automatic metric check (p95 latency, error rate, token burn) to decide expand to 8 reserved. If metrics are green at day 30, opt into Growth Slate. This reduces your initial spend while guaranteeing enough headroom for realistic traffic spikes.

I attached the PoC agenda: day 0-2 baseline tests, day 3-10 traffic ramp, day 14 review.

Call confirmed: Thu 15:00 PT works for me and Karthik; I've invited Soojin to cover runtime tuning.

Quick internal calc and recommendation before tomorrow's call with AureonThera:

- Baseline assumptions: chat model p95 CPU/GPU profile indicates ~0.12 tokens/ms on our optimized kernel at 2k seq. Expected steady-state concurrency for their expected 50qps translates to ~6 effective GPUs at p95. Reranker adds another ~1.2 GPUs of instantaneous load.

- Recommendation change: set Conservative Pilot reserved to 6 GPUs (operational) with a 2-GPU burst window rather than 4 reserved. This keeps perceived latency headroom but reduces their reserved spend by ~25% in month 1. We'll note the operational distinction in the worksheet and present both cost lines.

- Risk/mitigation: if they push very spiky traffic during day 3-7 we should enable auto-burst (time-limited at 10m windows) and trigger an immediate chat if p95 latency > 600ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows. Also propose a one-time 24-hour warm-up extension (covered by us) to smooth cold-cache tail.

@Soojin — can you prepare a 1-slide appendix showing expected p95 curve vs GPUs for the PoC agenda?
@Kimberly — finance will need the adjusted month-1 invoices; I'll loop you in on the final quote.

Thanks,
